extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media critics, and readers interested in news coverage and media bias
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for recognizing, evaluating, and avoiding 'sanewashing'—the practice of normalizing or sanitizing radical, incoherent, or outrageous statements in news coverage—targeted at journalists and news consumers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Sanewashing
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanewashing is the act of minimizing the perceived radical aspects of a person or idea in order to make them appear more acceptable to a wider audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core definition used throughout the article; the term is applied to media practices that normalize radical or outrageous statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poynter definition: packaging radical statements to seem normal
rubrics_metrics.description: The Poynter Institute defines it as "the act of packaging radical and outrageous statements in a way that makes them seem normal", and suggests it is analogous to greenwashing or sportswashing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this analogy (greenwashing/sportswashing) when evaluating whether coverage is sanitizing or normalizing problematic speech rather than critically contextualizing it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator: rendering incoherent statements into cogent English
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters have a "tendency to render the Republican candidate's most bizarre and incoherent statements into cogent English, shearing off the crazy in a misleading manner" (Paul Farhi, The Atlantic).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for paraphrases or rewrites that strip incoherence, tangents, or alarming claims out of quotes and present them as coherent policy positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator: packaging ideas into news stories as if sensible suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that outlets are "packaging Trump's ideas into news stories as if they are sensible suggestions" (Kelly McBride discussing NPR).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the coverage treats an outrageous claim as a plausible policy proposal instead of highlighting its problematic nature or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator: leading with policy detail and omitting incoherence
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: choosing to headline a piece on an event with a specific policy detail while only briefly mentioning the speaker's incoherent or bizarre remarks, thereby downplaying them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate headline and lede choices—do they emphasize a sanitized angle and omit obvious incoherence or conspiratorial associations (example: NYT headline choice described in the article)?

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicator: imposing sense where there is none
rubrics_metrics.description: Critics say some coverage attempts to "impose sense where there is none" by rephrasing or reframing rambling statements into logical assertions (as alleged of AP/CNN/The Week coverage).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to headlines or summaries that transform rambling or non sequitur remarks into tidy talking points without showing primary evidence (quotes/clips).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cause: conventions and constraints of campaign journalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Sanewashing often occurs because "the normal conventions of campaign journalism do not account for candidates that do not stick to 'a certain pattern and a certain norm' of speech," and because time/space constraints make representing tangents difficult.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating coverage, consider structural causes—format limits, norms of paraphrase, and newsroom practices—that may unintentionally sanitize statements rather than conspiratorial intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: use the 'truth sandwich' technique
rubrics_metrics.description: Employ a 'truth sandwich'—to surround a lie or misstatement with the truth (developed by George Lakoff and promoted by Jay Rosen)—to avoid amplifying false claims while reporting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure coverage so truthful context frames any misstatements: lead with truth, report the false claim sparingly and in context, then reiterate the truth; recommended as a practical technique to avoid sanewashing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: let the quotes stand (use unfiltered quotes/clips)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poynter and other critics advise to "let the quotes stand" and for outlets to use more unfiltered quotes and clips of the subject rather than reinterpreting them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer verbatim, unedited audio/video/quotations when possible so audiences can judge coherence and content for themselves rather than relying on paraphrase or interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: point out lies and the purpose they serve
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should "point out the lies and also the purpose they serve" when reporting misleading or false statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identify falsehoods and explain why they are being used (e.g., to rally a base, deflect criticism), instead of neutrally repeating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedy: identify the journalistic purpose of including a quote
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists should "identify the journalistic purpose" of a quote before including it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask whether a quote illuminates facts, demonstrates a pattern, or merely provides color/appearance of balance; make that purpose clear to readers to avoid false equivalence or normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader responsibility: seek primary sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should "seek out primary sources" to counter sanewashing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage audiences to check original speeches, posts, and clips instead of relying solely on secondary summaries that may sanitize content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader responsibility: support outlets that prioritize accuracy over access or appearance of balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers should "support news outlets that prioritize accuracy over access or the appearance of 'balance'."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor and financially support outlets that emphasize factual accuracy and context rather than false balance or access-driven sanitization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting focus: continue coverage on patterns (e.g., mental fitness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advocated approach: continue to focus on stories such as a candidate's mental fitness and analyze speeches over time to surface patterns rather than isolated sanitized glimpses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sustained, analytical reporting (e.g., longitudinal pieces on speeches) can reveal recurring incoherence or concerning patterns that single sanitized items hide.
